cases.sentence: The sailors seem to have reached the island.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge each determiner with its nominal complement. The selecting determiner supplies the label of each resulting bare phrase structure; no independently stipulated bar levels are introduced. The subject denotes the sailors, and the object denotes the island. The plural noun sailors is treated as a whole lexical word rather than decomposed into separate number morphology. Both nominal objects are available for subsequent Merge.
derivationStages.statement: Build the two definite nominal objects.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge reached with the island, producing a structure labeled by V. Merge a silent thematic v with that structure, and then externally merge the sailors at the edge of the resulting v structure. This is the subject's first syntactic position, not a position supplied by seem. The analysis treats reach as a transitive predicate: the island is its Theme or endpoint, and the sailors is the participant introduced by thematic v. Reached is retained as a whole participial lexical form.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the lower predicate and introduce its thematic subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge perfect have with the lower v structure, labeling the result Perf. Then merge infinitival to as T above that structure. Perfect have licenses the participial form reached, while infinitival T licenses the base auxiliary form have. These are form-licensing dependencies, not additional syntactic movement or a decomposition of the input words. At this stage the subject remains in its thematic position. Infinitival T is assumed to require a subject at its edge but not to assign nominative Case; that requirement has not yet been satisfied.
derivationStages.statement: Add perfect aspect and infinitival T above the lower predicate.

relations.relation: Internal Merge to the infinitival subject position

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge the subject from its previously established thematic position to the edge of infinitival T. The resulting structure is labeled T. This analysis adopts an embedded EPP requirement, so raising proceeds through this position rather than directly from the thematic position to the matrix clause. The new occurrence and the lower occurrence are full copies of the same nominal object. The higher occurrence is currently pronounced, and the thematic occurrence is marked unpronounced. Infinitival to does not value the subject's Case, so the subject remains available for matrix agreement and further raising.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the embedded subject to the edge of infinitival T.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge seem with the completed infinitival clause. Seem selects a propositional complement and assigns no external theta role to the sailors: the apparent matrix subject receives its thematic interpretation only inside the lower predicate. Merge a silent, non-agentive matrix v above the seem structure, without introducing an external argument, and then merge silent present-tense T. The embedded subject remains at the infinitival edge in this workspace, providing an explicitly established source for the next raising step. English lexical seem stays below T; this analysis does not posit overt V-to-T movement.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix raising predicate and introduce finite T.

relations.relation: Internal Merge to the matrix subject position

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite matrix T first agrees with the accessible subject at the infinitival edge, acquiring third-person plural agreement and valuing the nominal's Case as nominative. Internally merge that subject at the matrix T edge to satisfy the matrix EPP. The newly created matrix occurrence is pronounced; the embedded-edge occurrence is now unpronounced, and the already silent thematic occurrence remains intact. Thus the derivation preserves a three-position raising chain without assigning an additional theta role in the matrix clause. Present tense and plural agreement license the whole-word form seem in its existing V position; the word is not split into separately realized morphological pieces. Finally, merge a silent declarative C with the completed matrix T structure. All branching is binary bare Merge, with labels supplied by the relevant heads rather than stipulated intermediate projection levels. The pronounced terminals yield exactly The sailors seem to have reached the island.
derivationStages.statement: Complete matrix agreement, subject raising, and the declarative clause.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative predicate ver ‘give’ projects a head-final VP with a dative recipient and an unpronounced object operator in its Theme position. The Agent, Öğretmenin, is base-generated in the nominalized clause's subject position, Spec-IP. The nominal inflectional head contains the nominalizer -DIK and third-person singular possessive agreement; together they license the genitive subject. Here Öğretmenin is therefore ‘the teacher’s’, not the homographic nominative expression ‘your teacher’, which would require additional genitive marking in this construction. Öğrencilere is the dative recipient. The relative clause's nominal inflection is not a finite past-tense head: the giving event's temporal interpretation is contextual. Kitaplar, the unaccusative matrix predicate kaybol ‘disappear’, and the matrix past-tense inflection remain separate objects. Whole-word nominal terminals already have their input associations; verbal stems and affixes have not yet received their collective surface realizations.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative clause's underlying argument structure and the remaining lexical material.

values.movement: left adjunction of V to nominal I

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb moves from its previously established VP position to the nominal inflectional head, leaving a head trace. Left adjunction to the head-final inflectional complex places the verb before the nominalizer and possessive agreement. This complex receives the collective realization verdiği through Turkish suffix allomorphy, vowel harmony, and intervocalic softening of the nominalizer's final consonant. The lexical verb and both suffixes remain distinct syntactic contributors. The null operator is still in the object position, so its later movement will begin from a position explicitly present in this workspace.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb into nominal inflection and establish the realization verdiği.

values.licensing: local government through the verbal head chain

values.interpretation: books that the teacher gives or gave to the students

derivationStages.stageRecord: A head-final CP is projected over the nominalized IP with an unpronounced relative complementizer. The null operator moves from its object position to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace and forming an A-bar chain. Its object trace retains the Theme interpretation and abstract accusative Case supplied by the relative verb chain; local verbal government licenses this argument trace. The CP is adjoined to the left of the nominal projection headed by kitaplar. Relative predication links that external head to the operator without treating the head noun as an occurrence moved out of the relative clause. The resulting modified NP is then merged as the internal Theme of the unaccusative matrix verb. No matrix external Agent is introduced.
derivationStages.statement: Form the object relative, attach it to kitaplar, and establish the matrix Theme position.

children.label: NP: null relative operator in Spec-CP

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix VP combines with the previously separate finite inflectional head to form a head-final IP. Because kaybol is unaccusative, its internal Theme cannot obtain structural accusative Case from the verb. The entire relative-modified NP therefore raises from the complement position shown in the preceding stage to Spec-IP, leaving an NP trace. Finite inflection licenses nominative Case on the raised NP, and the A-chain preserves its internal Theme role. The relative CP remains inside the moving NP; neither its operator nor its genitive subject moves into the matrix clause. The matrix verb remains in its lexical position at this stage, keeping NP movement distinct from the subsequent head movement and surface realization.
derivationStages.statement: Build the finite matrix IP and raise its internal argument to subject position.

children.label: NP: null relative operator in Spec-CP

values.movement: left adjunction of V to finite I

values.compatibility: Turkish permits nonplural verbal agreement with this inanimate plural subject

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb raises from its established VP position and left-adjoins to finite I, leaving a head trace. The stem kaybol and past suffix -DI collectively realize kayboldu; the third-person singular/default agreement exponent is zero. This agreement form is compatible with the inanimate plural subject kitaplar and does not make that subject syntactically singular. The completed matrix clause is represented as a root IP because the input provides no overt matrix complementizer or independent evidence requiring a further CP layer. The resulting pronunciation is Öğretmenin öğrencilere verdiği kitaplar kayboldu: the teacher is the genitive subject of the embedded giving predicate, the students are its recipients, and the relative-modified books are the Theme and surface subject of the past-tense disappearance predicate. Both movement chains retain their silent traces, and the relative operator remains unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix inflection and the surface analysis of the sentence.

children.label: NP: null relative operator in Spec-CP

cases.sentence: Which report did Nora file without reading?

values.interpretation: The report is the understood object of reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: On the parasitic-gap reading, the report is both filed and read. This derivation adopts sideward Internal Merge: the wh-object is first merged with reading and will subsequently be copied into the independently constructed matrix predicate. Merge Which with report, merge that object with reading, and introduce the gerund's external argument PRO with a silent verbal head. A silent nonfinite tense head completes the gerund selected by without. PRO remains in its thematic position because this nonfinite tense head has no subject-raising requirement. Reading is treated as an already inflected lexical item. The recursive labels are inherited from selecting heads; they do not represent independently supplied phrase-structure templates. The wh-object is provisionally pronounced here, before a higher occurrence exists.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the gerundive adjunct with the wh-object in its first thematic position.

values.copyPronunciation: Pronounce the matrix occurrence; leave the gerund-internal occurrence silent.
values.theoreticalCommitment: Sideward copying between separate workspace objects is permitted before adjunct attachment.

values.interpretation: Both object occurrences denote the same report.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Introduce file into a separate workspace object and internally merge a copy of the previously constructed wh-object as its complement. The gerundive adjunct and the matrix predicate have not yet been combined, so this is sideward movement, not extraction from an adjunct already embedded in the matrix clause. This implementation permits the same argument chain to receive the compatible Theme interpretations of reading and file. The new matrix occurrence provisionally carries the pronunciation, and the gerund-internal occurrence becomes silent. The two predicates remain separate workspace roots.
derivationStages.statement: Sideward Internal Merge supplies the matrix object's thematic position.

values.interpretation: The filing occurs without the corresponding reading by Nora.
Nora is the understood agent of reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Attach the without-phrase to the matrix verbal constituent, retaining the host's V label. This is event modification rather than a complement selected by file. Merge a silent transitive verbal head and externally merge Nora as its agent. Nora controls the gerund's PRO, so the understood reader is Nora. The matrix object does not c-command the adjunct from its present complement position; later wh-fronting will create an occurrence that c-commands both object positions. In this implementation, matrix v is not a Transfer boundary, so subsequent object movement does not require a v-edge intermediate copy.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the adjunct and introduce Nora as the matrix agent and controller.

values.copyPronunciation: Pronounce only the higher subject occurrence.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge finite past T, realized by the whole-word auxiliary did. It selects the bare matrix predicate file; no decomposition of did or reading into separate morphological terminals is assumed. T agrees with the previously merged subject and licenses nominative Case. Its subject requirement then triggers Internal Merge of Nora above T. Pronounce the higher subject occurrence and silence the thematic occurrence. Did is still in T at this stage, establishing the source position required for subsequent subject–auxiliary inversion.
derivationStages.statement: Build finite tense and raise Nora to the finite subject position.

values.copyPronunciation: Pronounce did in C, not in T.

values.interpretation: The filed report and the unread report are the same argument.
values.locality: Sideward copying preceded adjunct attachment; the final wh-occurrence c-commands both lower occurrences.

values.interpretation: Nora is both the filer and the understood reader.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge interrogative C above the finite clause. C's inversion requirement first moves did from its established T position into a complex C head. Its wh-requirement then internally merges the matrix object at the left edge of the clause. Pronounce the C occurrence of did and the highest occurrence of Which report, leaving their lower copies silent. The highest wh-occurrence c-commands both thematic object occurrences and unifies the sideward-copy dependency. Thus the reading gap is licensed together with the ordinary matrix object gap, rather than by extracting directly out of an attached adjunct. The subject's lower copy continues to control PRO. The sentence is grammatical on this analysis, under the stated sideward-movement and phase assumptions: it asks which report Nora filed without reading that report.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the interrogative and license the parasitic-gap reading.

cases.sentence: 花子が読んだ本を太郎が買った。

values.realization: The silent relative operator has no pronounced case particle.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded clause is constructed as a head-final IP. 花子 occupies the subject position, with が represented as the head of a case-marked KP. The verb 読む selects a silent nominal operator as its object; this is the position corresponding to the book that Hanako read. The subject is generated in Spec-IP, adopting the classical GB treatment of the external argument rather than a VP-internal-subject derivation. The past-tense I head follows VP. At this stage, 読む and abstract past tense have not yet received their collective surface realization as 読んだ. KP is used as a head-final extension of NP for overt Japanese case particles; bare nominal expressions themselves do not require a DP layer.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative clause's underlying subject–object–verb structure.

values.binding: The operator c-commands and binds the object trace.
values.government: The object trace is locally governed through the verbal head chain.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded verb raises from the previously established V position to the adjacent head-final I, leaving a silent head trace. This analysis adopts V-to-I adjunction for Japanese finite predicates; it does not treat the surface past form as an unanalyzed V terminal. A relative C projection is then constructed, and the silent object operator moves from its established complement position to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace. The operator binds that trace under c-command, and the trace remains locally governed by the verbal projection containing the verb's head chain. The operator movement is entirely within the embedded clause. The resulting CP denotes a predicate of the missing object, not a clause in which 本 itself has raised. Both the relative C and the operator are unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Form the finite relative CP through verb raising and silent-operator movement.

values.interpretation: book x such that Hanako read x

values.morphophonology: The past form of 読む has a nasal stem alternation and voiced past allomorph.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative CP is adjoined to N′ on the left of the nominal projection headed by 本, giving the externally headed interpretation ‘the book that Hanako read.’ The nominal head is identified with the variable bound by the relative operator; it is not another occurrence in the operator's movement chain. The resulting NP combines with accusative を to form the matrix object KP. This object is first placed in the complement position of 買う, following the underlying matrix subject 太郎が. Matrix past I is introduced above VP and licenses the subject's nominative Case. The completed embedded verb–tense complex now receives the collective realization 読んだ. The three supplied tokens 読, ん, and だ are orthographic portions of that inflected predicate, not three independently selected syntactic words. The lexical dictionary form and abstract tense remain in the tree, with their realization recorded collectively.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the relative clause to 本 and establish the matrix clause before scrambling.

values.binding: The scrambled KP c-commands and binds its complement-position trace.
values.government: The object trace remains locally governed through the matrix verbal head chain.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb raises from its established V position to past I, leaving a head trace. Independently, the complete accusative KP containing the relative clause and 本を scrambles from the previously established matrix object position to a position left-adjoined to IP. The lower IP retains 太郎が in Spec-IP, so this adjunction yields the observed object–subject–verb order without making the object the grammatical subject or treating を as a topic marker. The scrambling operation moves the whole case-marked nominal, not 本 alone and not the embedded clause by itself. A KP trace remains as the matrix verb's complement; the scrambled occurrence c-commands it, and the chain retains the object's original theta role and Case. A silent declarative C completes the matrix CP. Embedded operator binding is preserved inside the moved nominal. This is a clause-internal scrambling analysis; the order alone does not require a unique discourse interpretation.
derivationStages.statement: Derive the matrix object-first order and close the declarative CP.

values.morphophonology: The past form of 買う has a geminate stem alternation and the unvoiced past allomorph.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The already constructed matrix verb–tense complex receives the collective realization 買った: 買う has the geminate past stem followed by the unvoiced past ending. This establishes the association with the supplied tokens 買, っ, and た without adding separate syntactic words for the orthographic subdivisions. The syntax is unchanged because this final operation is morphophonological realization, not another movement or attachment. The earlier realization of 読んだ is retained. The completed analysis therefore reads ‘Taro bought the book that Hanako read.’ Every indexed input token is accounted for by an ordinary terminal or one of the two predicate-realization groups. The sentence-final punctuation is not an additional indexed input token.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the surface realization of the sentence.
The subject DP and the locative-modified verbal phrase are assembled.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The demonstrative heads the plural subject DP; alten modifies Bücher inside the nominal constituent. Hier is a locative adjunct to the verbal phrase rather than an object selected by liegen. At this point the verb remains in its lexical position.

derivationStages.statement: The subject enters the verbal domain.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject DP is merged in the specifier of a stative verbal projection. Its head is unpronounced. The locative adjunct remains inside the projection's VP complement.

derivationStages.statement: The verb reaches the verbal head, and tense is projected.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Liegen raises from its lexical position into the verbal head. Its lexical-position occurrence becomes unpronounced, while the new occurrence bears the verb's pronunciation. A silent T is then merged above the verbal projection. The subject remains in its original position.

derivationStages.statement: The finite verb reaches T and the subject reaches Spec-TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb raises from the verbal head to T; its occurrence in the verbal head becomes silent. The subject DP then moves from the verbal-domain specifier to Spec-TP. The lower DP copy is silent, and the higher copy supplies the pronounced subject. T carries present-tense, plural agreement with Bücher; liegen is treated as one whole-word finite terminal rather than as separately pronounced stem and inflection.

derivationStages.statement: V-to-C movement and subject fronting yield the German V2 clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A declarative C is projected. The finite verb raises from T to C, leaving its T occurrence silent. The subject moves from Spec-TP to Spec-CP, leaving its TP copy silent. Consequently Diese alten Bücher precedes the finite verb in C, while hier remains in the lower verbal phrase and follows the verb on the surface.

relations.relation: subject movement to the preverbal field

cases.sentence: Which portrait of herself did Mira say that Leila admired?

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines of with the reflexive herself, combines that phrase with portrait, and combines the resulting nominal with interrogative Which. The of phrase identifies the person depicted, rather than modifying the event of admiring. Admired selects this interrogative nominal as its object; transitive v introduces Leila as the external argument. Labels identify the selecting heads of bare, binary syntactic objects, not independently stipulated bar levels. Admired is retained as an ordinary inflected lexical terminal; its past-tense licensing will be established by embedded T. At this point the interrogative object and Leila occupy their thematic positions.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the embedded thematic domain and the portrait nominal.

values.pronunciation: only the highest current nominal occurrence is pronounced
values.trigger: interrogative escape through the transitive v edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies the object from its already constructed complement position to an outer edge of embedded v. This escape position keeps the interrogative nominal accessible when the transitive phase's complement is transferred. The lower occurrence retains the object's thematic structure but is unpronounced; the newly highest occurrence currently carries the nominal's pronunciation. The added edge is outside Leila's base position and is not the reconstruction site used for reflexive interpretation in this analysis.
derivationStages.statement: Move the interrogative nominal to the embedded v-phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent finite past T merges above the embedded v domain and agrees with Leila. Leila then internally merges into the subject position of T, leaving an unpronounced thematic copy. The lexical form admired expresses the embedded predicate's past inflection without a separate pronounced tense morpheme. Declarative that subsequently merges with the resulting T object. It is an overt complementizer, not the interrogative operator; the interrogative nominal remains at the v edge until the next stage.
derivationStages.statement: Complete embedded tense and introduce declarative that.

values.trigger: escape from the embedded declarative C phase

derivationStages.stageRecord: The declarative complementizer provides an escape edge for the nominal's long-distance interrogative dependency. Internal Merge copies the nominal from the embedded v edge to the edge of C, leaving the v-edge occurrence unpronounced. That remains overt. This intermediate C-edge occurrence is above the embedded subject, whereas the original object occurrence remains below it; that difference will matter for reconstruction and reflexive binding.
derivationStages.statement: Move the interrogative nominal to the embedded C-phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Say selects the completed declarative C object as its propositional complement. Matrix transitive v introduces Mira as the external argument. The interrogative nominal is consequently inside the complement selected by say, with its highest occurrence at the embedded C edge. Say is treated as a bridge predicate: its complement is not an extraction island in this derivation.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix thematic domain.

values.trigger: interrogative escape through the matrix transitive v edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge takes the nominal from the previously established embedded C edge to an outer edge of matrix v. This preserves accessibility across the matrix transitive phase. The embedded C-edge occurrence is now unpronounced but remains available for interpretation. The new v-edge occurrence is outside Mira's thematic position; movement therefore does not by itself establish reflexive binding by Mira.
derivationStages.statement: Move the interrogative nominal through the matrix v-phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite past T merges above matrix v and is supplied by the inflected auxiliary did. This analysis selects did as a whole-word T terminal, rather than decomposing its spelling into separate morphological objects. Auxiliary support leaves lexical say in its base form and provides a head capable of satisfying interrogative inversion. T agrees with Mira, and Mira internally merges from the thematic position into the T subject position. The lower subject copy is unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Establish matrix tense, auxiliary support, and the matrix subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent interrogative C merges with matrix T. Its inversion requirement then attracts the already present auxiliary did from T into a complex C head. The lower auxiliary occurrence is unpronounced, and the higher occurrence realizes did before Mira. This head dependency is distinct from the nominal's successive-cyclic movement; the nominal still occupies the matrix v edge.
derivationStages.statement: Create interrogative C and raise did into it.

values.interpretation: lowest-copy reconstruction of the portrait-of-herself restriction

values.licensing: embedded subject c-command and local binding at the reconstructed object occurrence

derivationStages.stageRecord: Interrogative C attracts the nominal from the matrix v edge to its final left-peripheral position. Only this highest nominal occurrence is pronounced. At interpretation, the interrogative operator takes matrix scope, but its portrait-of-herself restriction is interpreted at the original object occurrence. Leila in the embedded T subject position c-commands that occurrence and supplies the local antecedent of herself. This gives the reading asking which portrait of Leila Mira said Leila admired. Reconstruction is interpretation of a retained copy, not a new downward syntactic movement; the intermediate escape copies remain in the completed structure. This analysis commits to the low reconstruction option rather than the intermediate option that permits Mira as antecedent.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the question with lowest-copy reconstruction and binding by Leila.

cases.sentence: Which portrait of herself did Mira say that Leila admired?

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines of with herself, combines that phrase with portrait, and combines the resulting nominal with interrogative Which. The of phrase identifies the depicted person. Admired selects the nominal as its object, and transitive v introduces Leila as its external argument. Bare binary objects receive the labels of their selecting heads, without separate bar-level projections. Admired is a whole-word inflected terminal whose past-tense licensing will be established by embedded T. Both arguments are initially in their thematic positions. In this analysis, the nominal's restriction will ultimately be interpreted at an intermediate escape copy rather than at this original object occurrence.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the embedded thematic domain and the portrait nominal.

values.pronunciation: only the highest current nominal occurrence is pronounced
values.trigger: interrogative escape through the transitive v edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies the object from its established complement position to an outer edge of embedded v. The escape position preserves accessibility when the phase complement is transferred. The lower occurrence retains the thematic structure but becomes unpronounced; the new highest occurrence currently supplies pronunciation. This edge is outside Leila's base position and is only an escape position, not the chosen site for interpreting the reflexive.
derivationStages.statement: Move the interrogative nominal to the embedded v-phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent finite past T merges above embedded v and agrees with Leila. Leila internally merges into the T subject position, leaving its thematic copy unpronounced. Admired retains its whole-word lexical realization and is licensed as the past embedded predicate. Declarative that then merges with the completed T object. It introduces the reported proposition and does not itself take interrogative scope; the interrogative nominal still occupies the embedded v edge.
derivationStages.statement: Complete embedded tense and introduce declarative that.

values.trigger: escape from the embedded declarative C phase

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies the interrogative nominal from the embedded v edge to an escape edge of declarative C. The former highest occurrence becomes unpronounced, and that remains overt. The C-edge nominal is outside embedded T and therefore outside Leila's c-command domain. Once this C object is embedded under say, the matrix subject can c-command its edge. This is the intermediate occurrence selected for interpreting the portrait restriction in the Mira reading.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the embedded C-edge reconstruction position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Say selects the declarative C object as its propositional complement, and matrix transitive v introduces Mira as speaker. Mira now c-commands the embedded C-edge occurrence of the interrogative nominal. Because that occurrence is outside embedded T, Leila is below it rather than an intervening c-commanding subject. Say is analyzed as a bridge predicate whose declarative complement permits the interrogative dependency to continue.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix thematic domain containing the intermediate copy.

values.trigger: interrogative escape through the matrix transitive v edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge moves the nominal from the already established embedded C edge to an outer matrix v edge. This supplies the next phase escape position. The embedded C-edge copy becomes unpronounced but retains its internal portrait-of-herself structure for later interpretation. The matrix v-edge copy is higher than Mira's base position, so the antecedent reading is based on the retained embedded C-edge copy, not on this newly added escape position.
derivationStages.statement: Move the interrogative nominal through the matrix v-phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite past T merges above matrix v and is realized by the whole-word auxiliary did. Auxiliary support allows say to remain in its base form while furnishing the head required for interrogative inversion. T agrees with Mira, which then internally merges from its thematic position into the T subject position. Mira's lower copy becomes unpronounced. Its higher occurrence continues to c-command the retained embedded C-edge nominal.
derivationStages.statement: Establish matrix tense, auxiliary support, and the matrix subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent interrogative C first merges with matrix T and then attracts the already present auxiliary did into a complex C head. The T occurrence of did becomes unpronounced, while its C occurrence supplies the overt auxiliary before Mira. The nominal remains at the matrix v edge until the next stage. Auxiliary head movement and interrogative nominal movement are distinct dependencies.
derivationStages.statement: Create interrogative C and raise did into it.

values.interpretation: intermediate C-edge reconstruction of the portrait-of-herself restriction

values.licensing: matrix subject c-command of the picture nominal interpreted at the embedded C edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Interrogative C attracts the nominal from the matrix v edge to the final question position; only the highest nominal copy is pronounced. The interrogative operator takes matrix scope, but the portrait-of-herself restriction is interpreted at the retained embedded C-edge occurrence. Mira in the matrix T subject position c-commands that occurrence, whereas Leila does not. This analysis adopts the intermediate-reconstruction treatment of picture-noun anaphors: because the nominal has no internal subject and its interpreted occurrence is outside embedded T, Mira is the accessible subject antecedent at that site. The resulting reading asks which portrait of Mira Mira said Leila admired. This reading is dependent on permitting that picture-noun reconstruction option; a theory requiring obligatory lowest reconstruction would retain only the Leila reading. Copy interpretation does not move the nominal downward, and the lower thematic copy still provides the object dependency of admired.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the question with intermediate reconstruction and binding by Mira.

cases.sentence: Mia liest das Buch und Leo schreibt einen Brief.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The sentence coordinates two independent propositions: Mia reads the book, and Leo writes a letter. In this GB analysis, German VP and IP are underlyingly head-final, while the surface declaratives will be verb-second CPs. Each subject is generated in Spec-IP, the traditional GB external-argument position adopted here; no VP-internal subject movement is assumed. Each accusative object is the complement of its verb inside V′. Nominal arguments are DPs, with a silent D for each proper name. Finite I licenses nominative on its subject, and each transitive verb governs and assigns accusative to its object. The verbs are introduced as the inflected lexical forms liest and schreibt; abstract I bears matching present-tense and third-person singular features but is not a separately pronounced affix. Consequently, no morphological fusion or special token realization is required. The separate coordinator will eventually take the two completed CPs as its conjuncts.
derivationStages.statement: Construct two head-final German IPs and the coordinating head.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Each verb adjoins to its own finite I before movement to C. This intermediate workspace makes the successive-cyclic head-movement commitment explicit: neither verb skips the intervening inflectional head. The lower V positions become silent head traces, while the inflected lexical terminals are pronounced in the newly formed complex I heads. Their lexical forms already agree with the finite features of I; this movement does not concatenate or respell morphological pieces. The objects remain in their original complement positions, and the subjects remain in Spec-IP. The argument and Case dependencies established in the preceding stage are preserved through the verbal chains.
derivationStages.statement: Raise each finite verb from V to I, retaining its VP-internal trace.

constraints: V2 satisfied independently in both conjuncts
theta criterion and Case Filter satisfied
local movement chains satisfy the ECP

derivationStages.stageRecord: A head-initial C projection is built above each existing IP. Each complex finite I head moves to its local C, leaving an I trace, and each subject moves from its already established Spec-IP position to Spec-CP, leaving an A′-bound DP trace. These local operations produce one constituent before the finite verb in each conjunct: Mia before liest, and Leo before schreibt. Subject fronting here is a structural Vorfeld operation and does not require a contrastive-topic interpretation. The head chains proceed through V, I, and C without skipping a head; under the adopted GB treatment, the local head traces and subject traces meet the ECP. The subject chains retain the nominative Case and external theta roles licensed at their lower positions, and the objects retain accusative and their internal theta roles. The two completed CPs are then combined in an X-bar coordination projection: the first CP occupies Spec-&P, und heads &′, and the second CP is its complement. This is full clausal coordination, not gapping or shared-argument coordination; all movement is internal to a conjunct and creates no extraction from a coordinate island. The proper-name DPs are referential expressions and have no coindexed c-commanding antecedent, so Condition C is respected; there are no overt anaphors or pronouns requiring Conditions A or B. The completed structure is grammatical and yields exactly the supplied nine tokens, with no punctuation terminal because punctuation is absent from the token list.
